name: Facial Texture Transfer Detection
description: Detects signs of face texture transfer operations used in face swapping and reenactment deepfakes — texture warping introduces distinctive spatial-frequency artifacts.
mechanism:
This method detects face texture transfer, the process by which a source face's appearance is mapped onto a target face's geometry — a core operation in face swap and face reenactment deepfakes:

1. **UV Mapping Artifact Detection**: Face texture transfer involves mapping the source face texture onto the target face geometry via UV (texture coordinate) mapping, typically using a 3D Morphable Model (3DMM). This process introduces characteristic artifacts: (a) texture stretching near UV seams (particularly along the jawline and hairline where 3DMM mesh density is lowest), (b) interpolation artifacts from bilinear/bicubic resampling of the source texture at non-integer UV coordinates, (c) resolution mismatches between the source face texture and the target face geometry rendering. The method detects these artifacts by analyzing the local spatial frequency content — UV stretching creates directional frequency attenuation, visible as anisotropic blurring in specific face regions.

2. **Pore and Micro-Texture Consistency Analysis**: Real faces have consistent micro-texture — skin pores, fine wrinkles, and peach fuzz — that follows the 3D surface geometry of the face. In texture transfer, the source face's micro-texture is projected onto a different face geometry, creating inconsistencies: pores appear at wrong angles relative to the local surface normal, micro-texture scale varies unnaturally across the face (stretched in areas where the source and target face shapes differ most), and pore orientation does not follow the natural radial pattern from the nose center. The method quantifies these inconsistencies by comparing detected pore orientations with expected orientations from the estimated 3D face shape.

3. **Color Transfer Boundary Detection**: Texture transfer deepfakes must harmonize the color statistics of the source face with the target video's lighting and skin tone. This color transfer (often histogram matching or neural style transfer) leaves boundaries where the color-corrected face region meets the original skin. The method detects these boundaries by analyzing the local color distribution statistics — mean, variance, and skewness of L*a*b* channels — in concentric zones around the face center. Authentic faces show smooth statistical transitions; texture-transferred faces show statistically significant jumps at the transfer boundary.

4. **Temporal Texture Coherence in Video**: In video, texture transfer is applied frame-by-frame, and slight variations in face alignment, UV mapping, and color correction create temporal texture inconsistencies. The method tracks texture patches across frames and measures: (a) texture phase coherence — consistent high-frequency phase relationships should persist across frames for real faces, (b) color correction stability — the color transfer parameters should not vary significantly between adjacent frames, (c) micro-texture persistence — real pores and fine wrinkles maintain their relative positions across frames; texture transfer may produce slightly different micro-detail per frame due to interpolation variations.
parameters:
3DMM for UV mapping: BFM 2009 with 53,490 vertices
Pore detection: Gabor filters at 4 orientations, σ = 2 pixels
Color analysis: L*a*b* color space, concentric zone width 8 pixels
Texture patch tracking: 16×16 pixel patches, SSIM metric
Phase coherence window: 10 consecutive frames
Minimum face resolution: 128×128 pixels
UV stretching threshold: anisotropy ratio > 1.5
Color boundary detection: KL divergence > 0.1 between adjacent zones
accuracy: 81–89% accuracy detecting face texture transfer artifacts. UV mapping artifact detection achieves AUC of 0.87 on FaceShifter and FSGAN datasets. Pore consistency analysis provides F1-score of 0.84. Color boundary detection is effective for face swaps but less effective for full-face generation. Temporal texture coherence adds 4–6% improvement in video analysis.
source: Nirkin, Y. et al. (2019). FSGAN: Subject Agnostic Face Swapping and Reenactment. Proceedings of ICCV, 7184–7193.
useCase: Detecting face swap deepfakes that rely on texture transfer. Identifying face reenactment manipulations in video. Forensic analysis of suspected deepfake evidence. Evaluating quality of face compositing in visual effects.
strengths:
• Targets the core mechanism of face swap deepfakes — texture transfer
• Pore and micro-texture analysis exploits fundamental geometric inconsistencies
• Color boundary detection works independently of generation quality
• Temporal analysis provides video-specific enhancement
• UV mapping artifacts are intrinsic to 3DMM-based face swaps and hard to eliminate
limitations:
• Full-face generation (StyleGAN, diffusion models) does not use texture transfer — method not applicable
• Low-resolution video lacks sufficient pore and micro-texture information
• Heavy compression destroys fine-detail forensic signals
• Advanced neural rendering may bypass explicit UV mapping step
• Makeup and skin filters naturally alter micro-texture and may trigger false positives
